# University of the Andes (Colombia) - Summary
Founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón and others as Colombia’s first nonsectarian and politically neutral university, University of the Andes (Uniandes) began classes in 1949 with 80 students. Modeled after the American university system, it aimed to educate professionals combining technical expertise with liberal education to serve Colombia’s development. Situated in Bogotá’s historic center, the main campus blends renovated industrial and religious buildings with modern facilities totaling over 180,000 square meters, including classrooms, labs, five specialized libraries, and sports centers such as the iconic La Caneca. The campus environment is enriched by nearby cultural institutions and government offices. Its unique mascot—a goat named Seneca—symbolizes the university’s spirit and tradition.
Uniandes is governed by a Board of Trustees overseeing general policy and a Board of Directors managing administration. The academic structure consists of 14 units—10 faculties and specialized centers—offering interdisciplinary programs that allow student-designed curricula. Notably, 70% of the full-time faculty hold PhDs from top global universities. The student body is highly competitive, with 95% ranking in Colombia’s top 1% of high school graduates, and includes a significant international component via extensive exchange programs. Alumni include prominent political leaders such as former Colombian President César Gaviria and key ministers, alongside noted figures in academia, arts, and sciences.
